dataset.name: Leaf sample details, leaf traits by age, Feb2017, PA-SLZ: Panama
description: This data package contains details of leaves sampled for leaf water potential and gas exchange measurements from the Bosque Protector San Lorenzo (PA-SLZ) NGEE Tropics site in Panama during February of 2017. The sunlit canopy leaves of Apeiba membranacea (APEIME), Guatteria dumetorum (GUATDU), Miconia borealis (MICOBO), Terminalia amazonia (TERMAM), Virola multiflora (VIROSP) and Vochysia ferruginea (VOCHFE) species were collected before dawn and around midday. Data for each sample includes species, age, sample number and a photograph. Within the attached zip file are three Excel files, two containing metadata and a single file with leaf sample data "2017_SLZ_LeafSamples_ByAgeV4.xlsx." Leaf sample photographs are included in "2017_SLZ_LeafSample_PhotosV2.zip". The leaf sampling protocol is described in "NGEE_Tropics_BNL_Leaf_Sample_Protocol.pdf." This data was collected as part of the 2017 BNL–STRI leaf traits by age campaign. See related datasets for leaf water potential, leaf spectra, sap flow, LMA, gas exchange and leaf chemistry. Note that this data packages was updated in May, 2021. The original data package was missing sample photographs. This has been corrected in NGT0045_2017_SLZ_LeafSamples_ByAgeV4.zip.
This dataset was originally published on the NGEE Tropics Archive and is being mirrored on ESS-DIVE for long-term archival

spatialCoverage.description: Site Name: Bosque Protector San Lorenzo (Fort Sherman). Site ID: PA-SLZ. Located in Panama. Established in 1997, the FTS canopy crane is located approximately 11km South West from the city of Colon, in the middle theParque Natural San Lorenzo (formerly known as FortSherman) and is surrounded by 300-year old, low-landtropical rainforest. The crane is 52 meters tall with aradius of 54 meters, and can reach approximately 240species of trees and lianas. (Paton 2015 FTS Met report) For more information on this site, visit: http://biogeodb.stri.si.edu/physical_monitoring/research/sherman,http://www.stri.si.edu/english/research/facilities/terrestrial/cranes/cranes_and_sites.php Site contact(s): (Argelis Ruiz <ruiza@si.edu>)
